newsitem.title: USA: US nonfinancial debt growth sped up in Q1.
newsitem.headline: US nonfinancial debt growth sped up in Q1.

text.p: Total debt held by U.S. households, businesses and federal, state and local governments grew at a 5.2 percent annual rate in the first three months this year, the Federal Reserve said on Thursday.
That was a pickup from a revised 4.8 percent rate of increase registered in the final quarter last year. The Fed had previously said fourth-quarter debt grew more slowly at a 4.5 percent rate.
Growth of federal government debt eased to a 2.5 percent annual rate in the first quarter from 3.1 percent, partly because of a falling government budget deficit, the Fed said.

But debt in non-federal government sectors -- businesses, households and state and local governments -- accelerated to a 6.2 percent annual rate of increase in the first quarter from 5.4 percent in last year's final quarter.
Nonfinancial debt represents borrowings by all economic sectors except banks, thrifts, finance companies and otheer financial services providers.

"Business debt growth rose in the first quarter, with an increase in borrowing from banks accounting for most of the pickup," the Fed said. It also noted state and local government debt increased for a second consecutive quarter, rising at a 3.7 percent rate compared with 6.7 percent in the final three months of last year.
The Fed said it was the first time in three years that state and local government debt had grown for two consecutive quarters.
